subject: Batch request duplication — credit request for May spike
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex@kestrel.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Kestrel Finance <finance@kestrel.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected May usage spike — suspected duplicate batches

Hi Lauren,

We just received the May invoice and are seeing a ~2.2M token jump between our April and May embedding jobs that doesn't line up with our job logs. Our infra team is confident we only sent the usual daily batches; the spike looks like duplicate processing on Redwood's side. The overage on our bill is ~USD 7,200.

Can you please:
- Share the raw usage lines for May 11–13 for project kestrel-prod?
- Tell us how duplicates are detected and whether you can issue a credit if it was counted twice by your system?

I’m attaching a small export of the Kestrel side traces. We can jump on a call if helpful — we need to get traction on this before the end of week.

Thanks,
Alex Monroe
Head of ML Infrastructure
Kestrel Systems

[Attachment: kestrel-export-sample.csv]
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Kestrel Finance <finance@kestrel.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected May usage spike — suspected duplicate batches

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample export. Sorry for the disruption. I’m looping in Karthik from infra and Marcus from billing so we can triage and propose a remediation/credit.

Karthik: can you please pull the server-side request logs and look specifically for identical batch payloads / retry artifacts between May 11–13 for project kestrel-prod?
Marcus: once we have a confirmed duplicate-count, what’s the standard workflow for issuing a one-time pro forma credit and adjusting the May invoice?

I’ll coordinate with Alex’s finance team to make sure we have the right accounting information for the adjustment.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
phone: +1 415-555-0199
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Alex Monroe <alex@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected May usage spike — suspected duplicate batches

Hi all — I pulled request traces and ran a de-duplication audit. Short version: we observed a replay pattern caused by our autoscale retry window combined with non-idempotent batch IDs from the Kestrel SDK during a transient network flapping event on May 11 02:42–03:15 UTC. That resulted in 1,042,000 tokens being counted twice for the project kestrel-prod.

What I’m attaching: a compact audit PDF showing the duplicate request IDs (redacted), a CSV with the request_id / timestamp / token_count lines we see on our side, and a .zip with the raw logs we referenced. The Kestrel sample you sent helped pair up request_ids.

Proposed remediation:
- Refund calculation: refund token_count = 1,042,000 tokens (deduped) -> pro-rated credit of USD 1,780.80 (per Kestrel’s pricing tier on file).
- Process: billing issues a one-time credit against the May invoice; internal adjustment id: INV-RED-20270514-01.
- Engineering action: we’ll push a small SDK guidance note and add additional idempotency checks on the autoscaler.

Attachments included: redwood-audit-report.pdf, sample-usage-export.csv (matched lines), request-logs.zip.

Let me know if you need a deeper walk-through of the trace.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Alex Monroe <alex@kestrel.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected May usage spike — suspected duplicate batches

Alex / Kestrel Finance — I reviewed the audit and the duplicate token calculation from Karthik. Billing is prepared to issue the one-time credit as proposed. Implementation details:

- Credit amount: USD 1,780.80 (one-time credit applied to account).
- Invoice adjustment: we will create a credit memo and apply it to invoice #20270501-RW (May). The ledger entry will show INV-RED-20270514-01 as the reference.
- Timeline: credit memo will be created by EOD May 14 PT and reflected on your account within 24–48 hours.
- Tax/VAT: this will be treated as an invoice-level adjustment; we will include the VAT reversal lines on the updated invoice and provide an updated export if you need it for your records.

Questions for your finance team: what billing contact/email should we send the updated PDF invoice to? Also confirm if you want the credit applied against the current outstanding balance or to be left as a pre-paid balance for June.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@kestrel.ai>, Kestrel Finance <finance@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected May usage spike — suspected duplicate batches

Alex / Kestrel Finance —

Thanks for confirming. Per your preference on the call earlier today, Marcus will apply the USD 1,780.80 credit to your outstanding May balance (so you’ll see the updated invoice PDF with the VAT reversal lines). Marcus — please send the updated invoice to finance@kestrel.ai and copy me.

Alex — we’ll follow up with a brief SDK note and a short postmortem next week about the idempotency guidance. Appreciate you raising this quickly and for working with Karthik to validate the traces.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
